critiques.title: Avoid using the same dash pattern for two different declining species
critiques.issue: The trend chart uses identical dashed lines for House Sparrow and Starling, so the non-color cue does not distinguish those two series from each other.
critiques.rationale: Because the chart already relies on color plus line style, the secondary cue needs to uniquely identify each series rather than collapsing two categories into the same pattern.
critiques.evidence: The strokeDash scale maps both House Sparrow and Starling to [6,3], while Blue Tit uses a solid line.
critiques.suggestion: Assign a distinct dash pattern to each species so readers can separate the two declining lines even without relying on color.

critiques.title: Give the long-term trend the dominant position
critiques.issue: The ranking chart currently occupies the largest area, while the long-term population trend—the part that carries the conservation message—appears smaller and visually secondary.
critiques.rationale: If the story is about which familiar birds are declining, the trend view should own the strongest visual emphasis and the supporting views should frame it.

critiques.rationale: When the story depends on long-term change up to the present endpoint, omitting the final tick makes the latest observation slightly harder to read and explain.

critiques.title: Document when illustrative data should be replaced or refreshed

critiques.suggestion: Set a simple authoring rule for this graphic: confirm source status before publication and define who replaces illustrative values with final data.
